scope: Read-only source review of candidate c594c021: src/song-stage.js, src/journey-finale.js, src/places.js, src/audio.js, and supporting phrase/theme/voice definitions in src/journey-pulse.js and src/song.js. scoreBasis.audio: Technical structure only: ordered personal recall, staged layer entrances, shared scale/tempo, a separately gated full-output pause, and a terminal theme. This score says nothing about enjoyment, timbre quality, balance, loudness, emotional impact, or perceptual musicality.
scoreBasis.creativity: Source-observed design: eleven earned places become musical layers; retained player timing becomes an attributed phrase in the finale, followed by a recurring theme. The fixed theme and chord-tone projection limit melodic individuality.
scoreBasis.sensation: Unobserved: code and fixture screenshots cannot establish felt ownership, affect, or the sensation of playing/listening.
scoreBasis.cohesion: Source-observed coupling among place rewards, saved notes, World scale/clock, chapter labels, ring entrances, and finale order. Reduced by the intentional Journey voicing's loss of theme intervals and by synthetic ring pulses during rests.
scoreBasis.polish: Scoped source review of finale scheduling, persistence, caption timing, silence routing, and exits. No execution or device verification; identified ring-pulse mismatch prevents a higher assessment.

strengths.observation: Successful notes retain pitch, bar step, and absolute sequencer tick; completion commits the phrase with its rewards and rolls back on a failed save. Recall preserves note order and bar phase, while shortening exceptionally long rests by whole bars. Player contribution has a concrete durable representation.

strengths.evidence: src/song-stage.js:47; src/song-stage.js:61; src/song-stage.js:63; src/song-stage.js:95; src/song-stage.js:106; src/audio.js:70
strengths.observation: The full finale has a legible musical argument: earned entrances, named personal phrases, a bar of full-output silence, then the theme before credits. Playback joins the World's next downbeat and follows its scale and clock; visuals use estimated audible time. This integrates the reward with the existing musical system.

Ownership is explained at relevant moments: the round card says the phrase is retained, the ordinary song view explains that phrases arrive in the finale, and the finale names the current place's phrase. Journey phrases remain available when a place has not been replayed.

findings.observation: When an actual layer pulse decays to zero, the ring uses a synthetic sine pulse. All lit rings therefore continue visibly pulsing through the deliberately empty bar and through layer rests when reduced motion is off.
findings.consequence: The visual score no longer distinguishes an audible layer attack from silence, weakening the stated relationship between earned rings and their musical activity.
findings.remedy: For audible playback, return the actual pulse including zero; restrict any ambient fallback to an explicitly silent visualization. Keep rings steady throughout the intentional pause.

findings.observation: The Journey finale intentionally projects every recalled pitch and both theme passes onto the current triad. In the default major context, the theme's MIDI sequence 57,59,64,62,61,57 becomes 57,57,64,61,61,57 over the terminal tonic chord. Distinct theme degrees merge; the second pass deliberately repeats the same interpretation.
findings.consequence: The technical pitch contour presented as the recurring theme differs from the theme learned during play. Whether players still recognize it or feel ownership is untested; this is an intentional arrangement tradeoff, not a scheduling bug.
findings.remedy: Retain the theme's diatonic melody in the shared middle register, using the accompaniment to establish harmony; reserve chord-tone projection for selected recalled notes if desired. Validate recognition through actual listening before claiming success.

limits: No ears or people were used. Perceptual audio quality, emotional resolution, personal recognition, musical masking, and device reproduction remain unobserved.
